name: Terah
title: Abraham's brother and father of Lot
summary: Terah (also known as Tarah or Terak) was the son of Nahor and the father of Abram (Abraham), Nahor, and Haran. He took his family from Ur of the Chaldees toward Canaan but settled in Haran, where he died at the age of 205. He plays an important role as a link in the lineage from Shem to Abraham.

keyEvents.title: Terah's Lineage
keyEvents.description: Terah is mentioned in the genealogy from Shem to Abram as the son of Nahor and an important link in the line of the patriarchs.

keyEvents.title: Terah Becomes the Father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran
keyEvents.description: When Terah was 70 years old, he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran, three sons who would play central roles in biblical history.

keyEvents.title: Haran's Death in Ur
keyEvents.description: Terah's son Haran died in Ur of the Chaldeans, in his native land, while his father Terah was still alive. Haran left behind his son Lot.

keyEvents.title: Departure from Ur of the Chaldeans
keyEvents.description: Terah took Abram, Lot, and Sarai and set out from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan, but they stopped in Haran and settled there.

keyEvents.title: The Death of Terah in Haran
keyEvents.description: Terah died in Haran at the age of 205. After his death, God called Abram to leave and continue on to the promised land.

keyEvents.title: Joshua's Reference to Terah's Idolatry
keyEvents.description: Joshua reminds the people of Israel that their ancestors, including Terah, lived beyond the river and served other gods before God called Abraham.
